newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl says currency union will start on time in 99.
newsitem.headline: Kohl says currency union will start on time in 99.

text.p: European currency union will start as planned on January 1 1999, with the would-be members meeting membership criteria laid out in the Maastricht treaty, German Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Monday.
"The euro will come," said Kohl at a meeting of the leaders of his Christian Democratic party (CDU).
Kohl went on to say that he was sure that German economic growth in 1997 would be around 2.5 percent, and that growth would be stronger in 1998.

Higher growth would impact on Germany's jobless figures, Kohl said, with a turnaround in the trend in the German labour market likely to come towards the end of this year or the beginning of next year.
Germany's jobless rate rose in April to a seasonally adjusted 4.299 million, leading to further doubts about its ability to meet economic convergence criteria for EMU.

Kohl said that comments he made last week on a trip to New Zealand, where he said he saw no signs of a turnaround in the rising jobless trend this year, related to a turnaround in the average figure for the year.
He said that it was still the case that there was no sign of a turnaround in the average figure.
